title: Detecting Touch-Induced Calcium Dynamics With Live-Cell Imaging in Torenia Stigma
author: Xuan Zhou
license_note: PMC full-text XML — Bio-protocol — CC-BY confirmed in article XML
materials: Transgenic T. fournieri plants expressing the GCaMP6f-NES probe (UBIQUITIN 10 promoter) [12] produce flowers with open stigmas capable of normal movement; this probe can be used by other groups Reagents
Distilled water (Sangon Biotech, catalog number: E607017-
Absolute ethanol (Sangon Biotech, catalog number: A500737-
PCR tubes (200 μL) (Sangon Biotech, catalog number: F611542-
Microsurgical tissue forceps (Vetus, catalog number: SS-JP)
Sharp-point tungsten needles (ETRA, model: 0.1 mm × 25 mm)
Microscope slide (25 mm × 75 mm, 1–1.2 mm) (Citotest, catalog number: 10127105P-G)

steps.title: Select motile flowers
steps.instruction: Choose flowers whose stigmas retain normal motility; the optimal stage is when the two pairs of anthers have not yet turned yellow (Fig 1A). Avoid unopened stigmas (no closure) and aged stigmas (reduced movement).

steps.title: Prepare water‑filled PCR tubes
steps.instruction: Label ten 200 µL PCR centrifuge tubes (Sangon Biotech, catalog F611542-0001) and add 150 µL distilled water (Sangon Biotech, catalog E607017-0500) to each tube.

steps.title: Cut pedicels and immerse flowers
steps.instruction: Using sharp scissors (Sangon Biotech, catalog F519231-0001), cut the pedicel tip of each selected flower and immediately insert the cut end into a water‑filled tube. Prepare ten flowers this way. Under these in‑vitro conditions the excised stigmas remain suitable for calcium imaging for 12 h at 25–30 °C, 40–80 % relative humidity, and 300–500 lx.

steps.title: Build slide mounting platform
steps.instruction: Stack five microscope slides (25 mm × 75 mm, 1–1.2 mm thick, Citotest, catalog 10127105P‑G) longitudinally and secure both ends with single‑sided tape (Scotch, catalog 810‑CQ33) to prevent sliding.

steps.title: Apply double‑sided tape
steps.instruction: Apply a 20 cm × 1 cm strip of double‑sided tape (3M, catalog 55236) to the center of the top slide, then peel off one side to expose an adhesive surface for mounting the stigma.

steps.title: Mount style and stigma
steps.instruction: Extract an in‑vitro‑cultured flower, hold the pedicel, and with microsurgical tissue forceps (Vetus, catalog SS‑JP) insert the tips ≈1 cm below the sepal apex and swiftly pinch off the style. Grip the style with forceps and press it onto the adhesive surface, orienting the inner surface of the stigma lobes upward so that the junction between lobes and style extends ≈5 mm beyond the platform edge. Apply 100 µL distilled water to the wound on the tape surface to keep the tissue alive. The stigma may be mounted upright (Fig 1D) or on its side (Fig 1E) depending on the observation goal.

steps.title: Set microscope for whole‑lobe imaging
steps.instruction: Place the platform under the microscope objective. Using 20× magnification, focus on the inner surface of the upper lobe in brightfield. Illuminate with a 130 W, 488 nm excitation source, set exposure to 80 ms, gain to 8×, and adjust any other parameters until the lobe outline is clearly visible in the fluorescence channel; frame rate and imaging duration will adjust automatically.

steps.title: Touch whole stigma lobe
steps.instruction: Clean a sharp‑point tungsten needle (ETRA, 0.1 mm × 25 mm) with absolute ethanol (Sangon Biotech, catalog A500737-0005). Start recording, position the needle tip near but not touching the stigma within the field of view, then advance the needle at ~45° relative to the inner surface, briefly touch the stigma until it bends ≈70°, and rapidly retract the needle along its axis. Keep the needle on the stigma for ≤500 ms. After recording, remove the style and stigma with forceps before proceeding to the next sample.

steps.title: Mount for single‑cell imaging
steps.instruction: For imaging individual papilla cells, mount the style on its side (Fig 1E) so that marginal papilla cells are exposed. Using 50× magnification, locate a clearly visible marginal papilla cell and adjust imaging settings to minimize background fluorescence.

steps.title: Touch individual papilla cell
steps.instruction: Clean the tungsten needle with ethanol, begin recording, position the needle tip near the target papilla cell, gently advance to make brief contact with the cell apex, then quickly retract. After recording, remove the sample as described in the whole‑lobe step.
